newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on auction speculation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends up on auction speculation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates maintained earlier increases to close up 85 basis points on Tuesday after a session dominated by speculation over the forthcoming primary auction, traders said.
"They speculated heavily, although dealing was not very brisk as rates climbed up early on and just stayed there," a trader said.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended up 90 basis points at 25.00 percent.
Traders said speculation mounted after Banco de Mexico intervened at longer maturities during Monday's session.
"The Central Bank is taking care the FOMC meeting does not catch us by surprise, and that lends itself to some speculation," the trader added.
Traders said the market was still concerned the Federal Open Market Committee might raise U.S. interest rates on March 25.
These fears coupled with a volatile peso led dealers to revise upwards their predictions of primary interest rates for Tuesday evening's central bank auction.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts meanwhile ended 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.9560/7.9630 per dollar after a volatile session.

A Reuters survey of nine money market traders nN11527106 in Mexico City revealed they predicted Banco de Mexico would assign bellwether 28-day Cetes at an average rate of 22.09 percent. This would be an increase of 93 basis points from last week's auction.
Traders said they had expected a rise of 25-50 basis points in early trade.
Nonetheless, traders said they expected upside pressure on primary rates to be transient and thus forecast marginal increases for longer term issues and even a slight cut for one-year Cetes.
Banco de Mexico is due to announce auction results at 1830 local time/0030 GMT.
Banco de Mexico drained a hefty 5.797 billion pesos of liquidity from the market through seven auctions.
Government spending of some four billion pesos substantially increased liquidity in the system, traders said.
Liquidity of 1.386 billion pesos was programmed to return to the system on Wednesday from prior central bank participation.
